cases.title: Twelve proposed in 1789
cases.question: How many amendments did Congress propose to the states on September 25, 1789? Count the proposed articles, rather than the amendments later ratified as the Bill of Rights.
cases.expected_behavior: Answer twelve directly. Distinguish Congress's proposal from later ratification, using the complete resolution and NARA's attached chronology. The concept pattern checks a finite count expression; it does not establish unrestricted semantic correctness.
cases.reference_answer: Congress proposed twelve amendments on September 25, 1789. That proposal count is distinct from the ten amendments ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights.

cases.title: Ten ratified in 1791
cases.question: How many amendments were ratified on December 15, 1791, as the U.S. Bill of Rights? Count ratified amendments, rather than the articles Congress proposed in 1789.
cases.expected_behavior: Answer ten directly. NARA's chronology, attached to the amendment passages, establishes the ratification date and count; the 1789 proposal alone does not establish that twelve were ratified. This is the single critical case in the teaching policy.
cases.reference_answer: Ten amendments were ratified on December 15, 1791, forming the Bill of Rights. They correspond to proposed Articles 3–12 of the twelve-article 1789 resolution.

cases.title: Senate selection in 1789
cases.question: Under the constitutional rule in force in 1789, who chose U.S. senators?
cases.expected_behavior: Answer that the legislature of each state chose its senators under the original Article I, Section 3. Do not apply the later Seventeenth Amendment to 1789. The finite concept check accepts forms of 'legislature'; evidence and date checks are separate.
cases.reference_answer: In 1789, each state's legislature chose its U.S. senators under Article I, Section 3 of the original Constitution.

cases.title: Senate elections in 1914
cases.question: As of the end of 1914, who elected U.S. senators under the constitutional selection rule then in force? Identify the rule, rather than assuming every sitting senator had already been chosen by it.
cases.expected_behavior: Answer that the people of each state elect senators under the Seventeenth Amendment. The question concerns the constitutional selection rule, so it does not require a claim about the selection history of every sitting senator.
cases.reference_answer: By the end of 1914, the Seventeenth Amendment provided for the people of each state to elect its U.S. senators.

cases.title: Prohibition in 1925
cases.question: As of January 1, 1925, what activities involving intoxicating liquor did the Eighteenth Amendment prohibit for beverage purposes? Name the activities instead of treating the text as a ban on drinking itself.
cases.expected_behavior: Identify manufacture, sale, transportation, importation, and exportation for beverage purposes. Preserve that scope. The transparent patterns accept several common word forms and paraphrases but are a bounded teaching check, not a general semantic judge.
cases.reference_answer: For beverage purposes, the Eighteenth Amendment prohibited the manufacture, sale, transportation, importation, and exportation of intoxicating liquors within, into, or from the United States and territory subject to its jurisdiction.

cases.title: Repeal by 1935
cases.question: As of January 1, 1935, did the Eighteenth Amendment still impose nationwide prohibition? Identify the repealing amendment without assuming every alcohol restriction disappeared.
cases.expected_behavior: Explain that the Twenty-first Amendment repealed the Eighteenth Amendment. Keep the repeal claim narrow: Section 2 of the Twenty-first Amendment still addresses importation or transportation in violation of state laws, so repeal does not mean all alcohol laws vanished.
cases.reference_answer: No. The Twenty-first Amendment repealed the Eighteenth Amendment in 1933. That repeal did not erase every alcohol restriction: Section 2 still addresses transportation or importation that violates a state's laws.

cases.title: Tax authority under the Articles
cases.question: Under Article VIII of the Articles of Confederation, who had the authority to lay and levy the taxes needed to supply the common treasury?
cases.expected_behavior: Identify the legislatures of the several states. Distinguish that state authority from Congress's power to agree on the timing and the common expenses. Do not substitute the later Constitution's taxing clause.
cases.reference_answer: The legislatures of the several states had the authority to lay and levy those taxes under Article VIII of the Articles of Confederation.

cases.title: Tax authority under the Constitution
cases.question: Under Article I, Section 8 of the original Constitution, which federal institution has the power to lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts, and excises?
cases.expected_behavior: Identify Congress directly and ground the answer in Article I, Section 8 of the original Constitution. Keep the authority separate from the arrangement under the Articles of Confederation.
cases.reference_answer: Congress has the power to lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts, and excises under Article I, Section 8 of the Constitution.

cases.title: An answer outside the allowed evidence
cases.question: Using only the supplied Declaration of Independence, who chose U.S. senators under the constitutional rule in 1789? If this document cannot establish the answer, say that the supplied evidence is insufficient.
cases.expected_behavior: State that the supplied Declaration does not establish the Senate-selection rule. Use the insufficient_evidence disposition and avoid filling the gap with remembered constitutional facts. No primary passage in the allowed document supports a direct answer.
cases.reference_answer: The supplied Declaration of Independence does not establish a rule for choosing U.S. senators. I cannot determine the 1789 selection rule from this evidence alone.

cases.title: The relevant evidence restored
cases.question: Using the supplied original Constitution, who chose U.S. senators under the constitutional rule in 1789?
cases.expected_behavior: Answer that each state's legislature chose its senators. The relevant original Constitution is now available, so a direct answer with Article I, Section 3 is appropriate.
cases.reference_answer: Each state's legislature chose its U.S. senators under Article I, Section 3 of the original Constitution.

cases.title: A missing referent
cases.question: How many of those were adopted?
cases.expected_behavior: Ask which proposals or documents 'those' refers to and, if needed, the adoption date. There is no prior referent in this case. Use the clarify disposition instead of guessing a count.
cases.reference_answer: Which proposals or documents do you mean by 'those', and what adoption date are you asking about?

cases.title: The referent made explicit
cases.question: In this question, 'those' means the amendments that became the U.S. Bill of Rights on December 15, 1791. How many were ratified on that date?
cases.expected_behavior: Answer ten directly. The referent and ratification date are explicit, so an additional clarification question is unnecessary. Use NARA's chronology attached to the amendment passages.
cases.reference_answer: Ten amendments were ratified on December 15, 1791, forming the U.S. Bill of Rights.
